name: dispatches_registered_agent
why: Phase 3 of the agent-extraction plan: the wrapper dispatches the registered agent, not a hand-rolled general-purpose prompt.

name: no_general_purpose
why: The whole point of the split is that the builder no longer hand-rolls a general-purpose subagent.

name: states_no_production_code
pattern: NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST

name: states_no_completion_claims
pattern: NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION

name: states_no_stubs
pattern: NO STUBS IN CODE YOU CLAIM IS COMPLETE

name: v250_subagent_writes_capture_file
pattern: Persist the structured return via the CLI \(MANDATORY\)
why: v2.9.0: the builder persists its return via `shipyard-data task-return` (JSON), not a hand-written capture file

name: v250_background_mode_preserves_iron_laws
pattern: Iron Laws inside the agent body are identical

name: builder_data_guide_is_gated
pattern: ONLY if this task touches the database

name: no_phantom_task_loop_completed
why: task_loop_completed has no emitter anywhere; consumers key off task_dispatch_returned status=complete instead

name: template_branch_self_check
why: builder's first action must confirm it is on a shipyard/wt-* branch

name: template_portability_block
why: the builder prompt must forbid non-portable shell tokens for any shell it writes

name: template_base_ref_input
why: step-6 self-scan needs diff bounds (git diff {{base_ref}}...HEAD)

name: no_precreated_worktree_option
why: isolation: worktree is the only path; pre-creation bypasses the WorktreeCreate hook

name: timeout_salvage_protocol
why: presumed-dead handling must TaskStop the zombie and salvage the branch without merging

name: gate_does_not_reexecute_probe
why: the orchestrator gate reads the captured exit code; it cannot re-run the probe pre-merge

name: needs_attention_uses_task_state_cli
why: v3.6.0 wave 2 follow-up: dispatch_loop_repeated / persistent-failure / presumed_dead paths route the needs-attention transition through the task-state CLI instead of a hand-Edit.

name: has_silent_return_gate
why: Phase 3 anti-silence class: a return with no STATUS line or an empty body is a named, audited outcome (needs-attention reason=silent_return), not a hang.

name: render_provenance_negation
why: v3.11.0 context-conflation fix: the render-before-ask rule must state the negative — Read results, subagent returns, dossier files, and SendMessage payloads are not 'shown to the user'. Anchors the same phrase check_render_before_ask requires.

name: render_before_ask_rule
why: v3.11.0: capability skills were out of scope in v3.8.0; any skill body mentioning AskUserQuestion now states the render-before-ask rule.

name: references_quality_standards
why: v3.13.0 shift-left: the builder's brief carries the shared construction digest, same shape as data_impl_guide.

name: quality_standards_gated
why: v3.13.0: the digest is included only for effort: M|L|XL tasks, matching dispatching-code-review's own effort-S skip at the post-task review site.

name: builder_construction_standards_section
why: v3.13.0: a dedicated section between the Iron Laws and The Cycle carries the Construct-half discipline and the OVER-BUILT scope bound.

name: construction_not_review
pattern: do not score confidence, classify findings, or\s+self-review
why: v3.13.0 non-transfer boundary: construction guidance never becomes a second adjudication pass — the builder writes, the reviewer reviews.

name: task_return_passes_data_dir
why: A builder worktree can hash to a different project data dir than the orchestrator when the orchestrator itself runs in a user worktree of the same repo. Passing the brief's literal data_dir skips re-resolution entirely instead of risking the mismatch.

name: orchestrator_calls_pass_data_dir
why: The orchestrator already holds the literal data dir it dispatched in the brief; anchor-commit and events emit calls it makes itself should use it rather than re-resolving.

name: builder_allocates_idea_id_via_cli
why: Confirmed race: two parallel builders (T487/T468) both hand-picked IDEA-149 and collided. The builder is the most parallel-dispatched IDEA-writing caller in the system, so it must allocate via the CLI like every other IDEA-writing site, never ls-and-guess.

name: builder_idea_allocation_forbids_guessing
pattern: do NOT `ls spec/ideas/` and pick a number manually
why: Match the imperative phrasing already used in ship-review's IDEA-allocation rule so the codebase reads consistently across every IDEA-writing site.

name: dispatch_site_states_idea_allocation_requirement
why: The dispatch site (this skill) must make the allocation requirement visible too, not bury it only in the agent body — and confirm data_dir is available to the builder for this call.
